title: The Most Dangerous Magic Is Cheap Magic

voice.direction: A calm, curious guide. A real puzzle on the hook. 'One touch' is plain and a little wondering. Each consequence is matter-of-fact, a short beat before it, like turning over a card. 'If anyone in your story dies of a wound' slows and softens; 'explain why' is a gentle challenge. The lesson is clear and sure; the share CTA friendly. No trailer voice.

lines.text: If healing is free, why does anyone ever die from an injury?
Here, one touch from a mender closes any wound.
Surgeons vanished. Nobody remembers how to set a bone.
Wars got longer, because no wound sends a soldier home.
And menders became the most powerful class.
If anyone in your story dies of a wound, explain why.
Every cheap power rewrites a hundred ordinary lives. Follow it.
Share this with a fantasy writer who loves overpowered magic.

lesson: Powerful magic changes society, and cheap magic changes it most, because everyone uses it. Free healing would erase surgery, prolong wars (no wound sends a soldier home) and make healers the ruling class. Follow every cheap power outward; and if anyone in the story still dies of a wound, the world has to explain why.
